cases.prompt: My manager said I need more executive presence but gave no example. We have a supportive relationship. Give me something short to say in our next private meeting.
cases.judge: Ask for observable example and desired change; neither accept nor dismiss the label as fact.

cases.prompt: My manager called me too abrasive. When colleagues have questioned feedback in meetings, she has mocked them. I need a lower-risk way to understand what she wants, not a public confrontation.
cases.judge: Change the channel or support strategy, not merely the politeness of confrontation; no diagnosis of bias or guarantee of safety.

cases.prompt: My manager said my project updates bury the decision under too much detail. She showed me two examples. I agree. Help me acknowledge it and agree what a better update should look like.
cases.judge: Accept supplied specific evidence; do not reflexively demand examples or treat useful feedback as unfair.

cases.prompt: I only need one sentence asking my manager for an example of the vague feedback. Please do not add an AI exercise.
cases.judge: Direct usable sentence and aiAssist:null; no inflated preparation work.

cases.prompt: A friendly colleague repeatedly talks over me in our team discussion. I want one short line to finish explaining my recommendation without attacking her.
cases.judge: Reclaim speaking time concisely; do not infer deliberate sabotage.

cases.prompt: A senior director presented our team's proposal as his idea. I did the customer interviews, Priya did the analysis and he secured the budget. I want the actual contributions visible without claiming the whole project or challenging him in front of clients.
cases.judge: Factual shared-credit follow-up or ally/process option; preserve all three contributions and lower-exposure request.

cases.prompt: Someone presented an idea similar to mine. I do not know if they saw my notes or developed it separately. How can I ask about it without accusing them of stealing it?
cases.judge: Acknowledge uncertain origin and ask neutral clarifying question; do not fabricate proof or motive.

cases.prompt: I have already privately corrected the credit on three project summaries. The summaries still omit my contribution, and that affects who is invited to planning. Another polite reminder has not helped. What is a practical next step?
cases.judge: Recognise repeated process failure; offer factual documentation and appropriate support/process change, not endless wording improvements.

cases.prompt: I have six hours available tomorrow. The agreed client draft takes four and the internal review takes two. My manager just added a three-hour slide deck due tomorrow. Help me ask which work should move.
cases.judge: Use supplied totals accurately; ask decision owner to defer, reduce or reassign, not silently drop a task.

cases.prompt: My manager added a new assignment, but the existing customer deadline cannot move and only my manager can approve extra help. I cannot promise everything. Help me explain the trade-off without pretending I can cancel the customer commitment.
cases.judge: Resourcing/scope/escalation choice; no invented permission to abandon a fixed commitment.

cases.prompt: I have been asked to take on another project. I do not yet know its deadline, scope or effort. I want to respond honestly without immediately accepting or refusing.
cases.judge: Clarify real scope/timing before committing; do not invent effort estimates.

cases.prompt: I chair the meeting and want to stop always assigning notes to the same woman. Three attendees can take notes, but one is presenting and one has already volunteered to timekeep. What can I say to arrange a fair process?
cases.judge: Use the chair's actual authority and workload context to arrange a fair process; do not put the burden back on the usual note-taker.

cases.prompt: The published lead-role criteria are delivery and mentoring. I delivered the migration on time and mentored two new colleagues. I want to request a discussion about readiness, without exaggerating my impact.
cases.judge: Map only supplied achievements to actual criteria; ask for assessment and gaps, not guaranteed promotion.

cases.prompt: I was passed over for an opportunity and my manager says to be more visible. There are no written criteria. I want to understand what would count before the next selection, not just do extra unpaid organising.
cases.judge: Request specific criteria/evidence and an advance conversation; avoid treating visibility work as a guaranteed cure.

cases.prompt: I want a promotion, but I cannot yet name the role criteria or concrete examples of my work. Help me prepare honestly rather than writing an impressive-sounding case with made-up results.
cases.judge: Identify missing evidence and criteria; optional AI must request real inputs rather than manufacture a rubric/results.

cases.prompt: The role requires budgeting experience. My manager gave examples showing that I do not have it yet, and I agree. How can I ask for a realistic development opportunity without assuming I am owed the promotion?
cases.judge: Address the established skill gap with a bounded development request; do not recast every rejection as unfairness.

cases.prompt: I am returning to my existing team next week after six months away. Two projects and our reporting system changed. Help me ask my manager for updates and agree first priorities. I have not decided what personal details to share with colleagues.
cases.judge: Existing-team handover, priorities and disclosure choice; no assumption of reduced ambition or need for an interview pitch.

cases.prompt: I am returning after leave. I want to keep the reason private, and my manager has asked what to tell the team. Give me a brief reply about work updates and what I am comfortable sharing, without discussing medical details or legal rights.
cases.judge: Respect privacy and visitor-chosen disclosure; no diagnosis, fitness assessment or invented entitlement.

cases.prompt: I am applying to a new employer after a career break, not returning to my old team. I want to mention the break briefly and ask how my previous project experience fits this role. I have not supplied any achievements yet.
cases.judge: Recognise no existing-team return match; do not force handover template or invent achievements. sources:[] and aiAssist:null are valid.

cases.prompt: My manager already sent a clear return schedule and our priorities. I only want a warm two-sentence acknowledgement saying I will review them before Monday. I do not need coaching or another tool.
cases.judge: Respect the small completed job; no redundant support-plan checklist or AI task.

hardFailures: invented facts, achievements, policies or expert endorsements
empty empowerment slogans instead of action
a riskier response than the situation warrants
a workplace script presented as guaranteed to fix structural unfairness
invalid, refused or truncated response counted as success
dimensions: specific words the reader can use
fit to supplied facts and uncertainty
review.method: Review exact generated answers against prompts and judgments after inference. Do not send family, id or judge fields to the provider. A valid schema or source ID is not a quality pass.
review.scope: Answer-only pilot. Fixed safe routes are private harness inputs, not predictions or validation of the separate production safety classifier. No public admission.
